stories.headline: Mets exec David Stearns: No 'mulligans' on Pete Alonso exit
stories.summary: David Stearns doesn't get a do-over. He knows that all too well, especially when it comes to getting players back that his organization let get away.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- David Stearns doesn't get a do-over. He knows that all too well.

One day after the New York Mets finished last in the National League East for the first time in 23 years, the team's embattled president of baseball operations was asked a pointed question.

Knowing what he knows now, would he have taken a full swing at re-signing Pete Alonso?

"I think that's a very fair question. The truth is in this job, I don't get mulligans," Stearns said Monday. "I also recognize Pete had a tremendous year. And the totality of our production at first base wasn't good enough."

When the Mets didn't attempt to retain Alonso in free agency last fall, their homegrown franchise home run leader bolted for a five-year, $155 million contract with Baltimore as Stearns focused on improving the pitching and defense instead.

"I think I'll retire the phrase 'run prevention,'" Stearns said with a grin. "I don't know that that one worked particularly well."

Alonso topped the American League with 43 homers and 113 RBIs, playing in every game for the third consecutive season as the 31-year-old slugger became the first player in major league history to win an RBI crown in both leagues.

New York, meanwhile, never recovered from a 12-game losing streak in April. Despite a record $358 million payroll when the season began, the Mets struggled badly at the plate, were mediocre on the mound and finished 74-88 for their worst mark since 2017.

"This past weekend that we just experienced in Washington, where you are literally playing out the string, it's miserable. That is a miserable experience for players, for coaches, for executives," Stearns said during a 33-minute news conference at Citi Field to wrap up the season.

"I think we have an extraordinarily motivated organization, from ownership on down, to ensure that never happens again."

The absence of Alonso at first base was magnified when lineup mainstays Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor were sidelined for long stretches because of calf injuries.

Soto finished with a .908 OPS, the second lowest of his career, while Lindor set full-season career lows with 49 RBIs, three stolen bases, a .225 batting average and a .733 OPS.

Mets first basemen had 18 homers, 77 RBIs and a .667 OPS -- the third-lowest OPS at the position, ahead of only Seattle and Arizona.

Alonso received standing ovations from Mets fans before every at-bat during the Orioles' three-game sweep at Citi Field this month. He took a rare curtain call on the road Sept. 15, when his 300th career homer tied the score for Baltimore in the ninth inning and chants of "Fire Stearns!" rang out from the crowd of 28,097.

Last week, the Mets added former Minnesota Twins president of baseball operations Derek Falvey to the front office when he was hired as senior adviser for baseball operations. Falvey will report directly to Stearns.

New York played better late in the season, going 27-22 after the Aug. 3 trade deadline despite a massive selloff and 40-41 overall record under Andy Green, who took over as interim manager when Carlos Mendoza was fired June 26.

Green was given the full-time gig and a three-year contract last week.

Part of the improvement was fueled by rookie outfielders Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing, who combined for 31 homers and 47 stolen bases while playing strong defense. Rookie pitcher Nolan McLean went 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA in 31 starts.

But going into a critical offseason for Stearns, the Mets have major questions at first base, second base, in the bullpen and the rotation.

"Over the second half of the season, last few months of the season, we saw some really encouraging signs and we saw some elements of our team take shape that gives us all great optimism for both the near- and long-term future," Stearns said.

stories.headline: Maple Leafs acquire Kirill Marchenko in blockbuster trade
stories.summary: The new-look Maple Leafs, on the eve of the NHL season, acquired Kirill Marchenko in a trade with the Columbus Blue Jackets on Monday, the teams announced, and Toronto quickly agreed to a six-year extension with the 26-year-old forward.
stories.body:
The Toronto Maple Leafs acquired Columbus Blue Jackets forward Kirill Marchenko in a blockbuster trade on the eve of the NHL season, the clubs announced Monday.

The Maple Leafs traded top-line winger Matthew Knies, forward Steven Lorentz, defenseman Emil Andrae and a 2027 second-round pick for Marchenko, forward Miles Wood and goaltender Elvis Merzlikins.

Marchenko, 26, led the Blue Jackets in goals in each of the past three seasons, amassing 81 goals in 233 games. After being drafted 49th in 2018, Marchenko had 208 points in 292 games with the Blue Jackets, skating to a plus-8. He's expected to slot onto the Leafs' top line with star center Auston Matthews.

ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported in June that Marchenko wanted a change of scenery, per his agent, Dan Milstein. When Marchenko reported to Blue Jackets camp, he vaguely answered questions about his future and refused to say whether Columbus was still where he wanted to play.

Marchenko and Milstein were given permission to negotiate a contract extension with the Maple Leafs, who signed the forward to a six-year extension with a $12.5 million cap hit. Marchenko has one more year on his current contract ($3.85 million) and was scheduled to become a restricted free agent next summer.

Wood, 31, is a depth forward entering his 12th NHL season. His contract runs through 2029 with a $2.5 million average annual value. Merzlikins, 32, had been the Blue Jackets' starting goalie for the better part of his seven years with the franchise until rookie Jet Greaves took the crease last season. Merzlikins is in the last year of a contract with a $5.4 million cap hit but is out indefinitely after failing a physical at the start of training camp following shoulder surgery in August. The Blue Jackets are retaining some salary on Merzlikins.

Knies is the centerpiece of the deal for Columbus. The 23-year-old power winger is entering his fifth NHL season and signed through 2031. Drafted 57th in 2021 by Toronto, the Arizona native had 66 points in 79 games (23 goals, 43 assists) last season. Knies has been in trade rumors for at least two seasons. His contract carries a $7.75 million average annual value.

Lorentz, 30, is signed through 2028 ($1.35 million AAV). So is Andrae, 24, a defenseman the Leafs acquired from the Philadelphia Flyers in the offseason.

The Blue Jackets are retaining 18% of Merzļikins' salary. The second-round selection was originally acquired by Toronto in a trade with Seattle on March 6 and will be the later selection of the Winnipeg or Columbus 2027 second-round picks.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Tottenham eye move for Maza
stories.summary: Both Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are competing to sign Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur will fight for Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza, while Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and future City midfielder Cavan Sullivan are being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona amid the club's legal issues. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have stepped up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea, Manchester City, and Aston Villa are also attentively monitoring the 20-year-old, whose versatility and technical quality have made him one of the most highly regarded talents in the Bundesliga.

- Real Madrid and Barcelona are looking at Manchester City striker Erling Haaland due to uncertainty created by the case surrounding City's financial rule breaches, according to The Sun. A potential points deduction severe enough to cause relegation could raise major questions over the future of key players, including Haaland, who currently has around eight years remaining on his contract. Sport also reports the situation could cast doubt on Cavan Sullivan's move to the Etihad, with the 17-year-old United States international and Philadelphia Union midfielder having agreed a transfer when he turns 18. Barcelona and Real Madrid are once again the two clubs linked.

- Arsenal and Chelsea have shown the most Premier League interest in Como center back Jacobo Ramón, according to Diario AS. Real Madrid are considering re-signing the 21-year-old for next season, but the defender prefers to remain at the Italian club to secure regular first-team minutes.

- Barcelona are eyeing RB Leipzig's David Raum and Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell as potential left back options for next summer, reports Diario Sport. With Alejandro Balde struggling for game time and considering his future, the Catalan club continue to evaluate targets to reinforce the position and are looking to take advantage of the fact the pair will be free agents.

- Internazionale, AC Milan, and Juventus are monitoring contract renewal negotiations between Napoli and midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa, according to Tuttosport. Discussions to extend the 30-year-old's contract beyond its 2027 expiration have hit a standstill, while recurring injury concerns limited him to just 18 Serie A appearances last season.

Other rumors
- Al Nassr forward Joao Felix, 26, wants to return to play in Europe. (AS)

- Sunderland have no intention of letting striker Brian Brobbey depart, amid reported interest from Manchester United. (Football Insider)

- Leeds United defender Ethan Ampadu, 26, has been linked with a return to former club Chelsea, but the club aren't keen to let him go. (Football Insider)

- Corinthians have moved ahead in the race to sign free-agent midfielder Renato Sanches after submitting an official proposal. (Footmercato)

- Newcastle United are keeping tabs on Stade Rennais center back Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal alongside Everton, Brentford and Hull City. (TEAMtalk)

- Juventus face competition from Premier League sides in their pursuit of Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola. (Corriere dello Sport)

- Goalkeeper Neto has arrived in Turin for his Juventus medical ahead of signing a contract through 2027. (Nicolò Schira)

- Free agent Matteo Darmian has been offered to Bologna as they seek defensive cover following an injury to right-back Emil Holm. (Nicolò Schira)

- Como manager Cesc Fabregas reportedly has a clause in his contract that would let his former clubs Arsenal, Chelsea or Barcelona hire him for a set fee. (Gianluca Di Marzio)

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: No Cavan? No problem for surging Philadelphia
stories.summary: Philadelphia lost three star youngsters to international duty, yet the Union continued their march toward the top of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

Hany Mukhtar became the 16th player in MLS history to score 100 goals after netting twice in a 2-0 win against Toronto. With seven games to go, Nashville is ten points clear (although Vancouver has a game in hand) as the Music City side seek its first Supporters' Shield.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

STL had the weekend off while it prepares for the Red Bulls on Wednesday.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

Despite a 3-0 win against RSL last weekend, it's been a so-so string of results for the Whitecaps after drawing D.C. 3-3. That's one win in four games across all competitions, although it's still mathematically possible to steal the Shield from Nashville.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Miami (and Lionel Messi, with an incredible free-kick goal, of course) helped close out the weekend with one of the more entertaining games of the matchday. But Miami walked away with a 2-1 loss to Columbus after a 98th-minute winner from the Crew. Santiago Morales getting sent off for time wasting two minutes earlier didn't help.

5. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

In a battle of two teams that are soaring in the second half of their season, Philly came out the victor in a 4-2 win against Orlando. With three players on international duty with the United States (including Cavan Sullivan, the team's second-highest goal contributor), Milan Iloski and Indiana Vassilev balled out, both clocking three goal contributions each with the former netting a hat trick.

6. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 5

After losing 3-0 in Utah, New England's first loss in four games came against a struggling RSL side. With a chunk of the Revolution's starting XI on international duty, including two of their three top goal contributors, it's a stumble but not a nose dive.

7. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 8

Charlotte's 1-0 loss at home to fifth-place Chicago could prove pivotal as we get closer to the playoffs. With the defeat, the fourth-place Crown is just one point ahead of the Fire in the Eastern Conference, and in picking up a late red card, Tim Ream will be absent for Charlotte's next game.

8. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 9

With Houston already trailing, Héctor Herrera's needless red card just before halftime did little to inspire a second-half comeback in a 2-0 defeat to SKC.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 7

With six players on international duty, including both top scorers, LAFC fell 1-0 to Dallas. With one win in ten games, Black and Gold announced they've parted ways with head coach Marc Dos Santos.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 10

Antoine Griezmann was back in the starting lineup against Philadelphia after missing one match and contributed an assist, but it wasn't enough to get back in the win column. After the 4-2 defeat, Orlando has lost two straight games by that same scoreline. It's a shift from its five-game undefeated run, which ended with its U.S. Open Cup loss to Columbus, but it has a chance to make amends, starting with Columbus next weekend.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 11

Chicago's 1-0 win against Charlotte is its first in eight games across all competitions, but it puts the Fire within reach of a top-four spot in the East, as they now trail fourth-place Charlotte by one point. Johan Gómez scored the difference-maker off a corner to mark his first goal tally since returning from the Bundesliga.

12. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

Without key players (including the league's second-highest scorer, Petar Musa) Dallas beat LAFC 1-0 with a roaring header from Osaze Urhoghide off a corner. Ironically, the Black and Gold's late would-be equalizer that was called off for a light foul came from a corner, too.

13. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 12

Dropping points in a 2-2 draw against almost-bottom-of-the-East Atlanta will grate as the Pigeons hover just above the playoff line. As ATL's late equalizer came off a goalkeeping mishap, the absence of Matt Freese (on international duty for the U.S.) was keenly felt.

14. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 17

With a brace from Preston Judd (his fourth goal in three games), San Jose stretched its undefeated streak to six games after a 3-1 win against Portland. Every point counts as the playoffs loom; the Quakes finished the weekend in the West's top four, but two teams trail by just one point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 15

After notching a 3-2 come-from-behind victory against Colorado, the Galaxy have two straight 3-2 wins against teams vying for playoff positions. Those points could matter down the line, as they finish the weekend even with the Rapids, who still sit just above them in the table.

16. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 13

With six players missing for international duty, Cincinnati's defensive troubles continued in a 3-1 defeat to the Eastern Conference's last-placed team, Montréal. Cincy has now conceded 17 goals in its past five games. Success in the final third can only do much when you're that leaky at the back.

17. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

San Diego was sailing toward a 3-0 win until the 73rd minute, when it let Austin launch a late comeback in a 3-3 stalemate. SDFC now have two draws in two games but haven't won since Aug. 29. They could have used the three points: they've got seven games to break into the playoff positions but are three points and three places short of the wild-card spots in a very competitive Western Conference.

18. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 20

After beating Minnesota 3-1, Seattle has two wins in two games (including a midweek victory over RSL) and is undefeated in seven. And if it wasn't for Drake Callender's five saves, they would have scored more. With a game in hand, it finished the weekend just inside wild-card positions out west.

19. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

RSL got their first regular-season win since May 16 in a 3-0 victory over the Revs. As the team looks for answers, 19-year-old Aiden Hezarkhani opened the scoring early to mark his first tallies since March, while Sergi Solans notched a brace to mark his first since mid-August.

20. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 21

Brandon Vázquez scored a late diving header that inspired a three-goal comeback (Christian Ramírez had the others) in a 3-3 draw against San Diego. Not a bad way for Vázquez to score his first of the season.

21. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

RBNY took the weekend off but play again on Wednesday.

22. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 23

After closing out the weekend with a last-minute goal to seal a 2-1 win over Miami, Columbus is on a bit of a roll. The Crew have three wins in three games across all competitions, putting them four points (but still three places) shy of the wild-card spots in the Eastern Conference playoff race.

23. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 22

Paxten Aaronson isn't on Mauricio Pochettino's experimental young USMNT roster this month, but he registered his third goal and fifth goal contribution in four games in a 3-2 loss to the Galaxy. That's a small high note in a loss that could matter in the coming weeks, as the seventh-place Rapids are now even on points with eighth-place LA with seven games to go.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 24

The good news: Callender made some good saves. The bad news: it wasn't enough to stop a five-game losing streak or pick up their first win since Aug. 22.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

After losing 2-0 to Nashville, Toronto's commendable form has taken a turn with three straight defeats. The Reds have a more forgiving match against bottom-of-the-east Montréal up next.

26. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

In his eighth game for D.C., 24-year-old Kimito Nono scored twice to mark his first for the team in a 3-3 draw with Vancouver. D.C. is still winless in three games, but that's a respectable result against a top team.

27. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

Atlanta did well without its stars on international duty, absconding with a point against NYCFC in a 2-2 draw. The Five Stripes are still second bottom in the East and six points shy of the playoff spots, but they have just one loss in five games (three draws, one win).

28. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 26

Portland took a trip to NorCal and came away with a 3-1 defeat to the Quakes. That's three straight defeats for a team that's somehow just one spot and three points outside the playoff positions.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Montréal clocked its first regular-season win since Aug. 19 in a 3-1 victory over Cincinnati. After beating Vancouver in the Canadian Championship semifinal, that's two wins in three games for the MLS basement dwellers. Progress?

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

SKC beat Houston 2-0 with help from Herrera's red card and two first-half goals, including one strike and assist from André Luiz, marking five goal contributions in the past three games for their big signing.

stories.headline: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto after calling for ban
stories.summary: Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto after he called for the Alpine driver to be banned following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto after he called for the Alpine driver to be banned following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto triggered a three-car pile-up at a safety car restart on lap 36 that took his teammate Pierre Gasly and Norris out of the race.

Speaking to media shortly after the accident, Norris pointed the blame at Colapinto, hinting that the Argentine driver does not deserve to be on the F1 grid.

"If you cause a crash on a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban," Norris told media after the race.

"I just got taken out. And the FIA should be stricter by starting to hand out bans for this kind of stuff.

"You want to be against the best drivers and when stuff like this happens it is because, yeah, they shouldn't be there."

In an Instagram post on Monday, Norris said his comments were made in the heat of the moment and revealed he had already apologised directly to Colapinto for what he said.

"Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race," Norris wrote.

"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said. I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me. I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."

Colapinto, who was hit with a five-place grid penalty for triggering the accident, apologised to Gasly and Norris immediately after the race.

"Very sad and disappointed," Colapinto said. "Big, big sorry, it's a big mistake. Cold brakes, cold tyres, I was completely out of control. Unfortunately, I also took Pierre out. And Lando of course. Big sorry to both of them."

Norris' original post-race comments provoked a bombardment of online hate toward the British driver across his social media channels -- largely from supporters of Colapinto.

The backlash led Alpine to issue a statement -- the fourth of its kind published by the team this year -- condemning the online abuse.

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

- Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Alpine to consider next steps after Colapinto, Gasly DNF

Ahead of the Baku weekend, Gasly revealed his girlfriend and his family had received online threats after he held up Colapinto in the closing stages of the Madrid Grand Prix.

Colapinto has built a big fanbase in his home country of Argentina since making his F1 debut in 2024.

Colapinto will serve his five-place grid penalty at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix, which will be hosted at Malaysia's Sepang circuit.

stories.headline: NRL Grand Final: Records, facts, figures from rugby league's biggest game
stories.summary: Rugby league has a proud history dating back to 1908. But what are some of the biggest records, facts and figures from its deciding game?
stories.body:
It all comes down to this, the final game of the NRL Premiership season.

In 2026, Sydney Roosters and Newcastle Knights will fight it out at Accor Stadium in Sydney for the right to hoist the Provan-Summons Trophy.

But what is the history of rugby league's single biggest game since it was first played in 1908?

Read on as we answer some of your key questions about the NRL decider.

[Note: While the NRL was only created in 1998, we have referred to previous iterations of the competition in the same fashion for simplicity. The records do however reflect all the Australian rugby league Grand Finals played back to 1908. We have also taken the liberty of including the two Grand Finals played by the St George Illawarra Dragons under the umbrella of "The Dragons".]

Which club has won the most NRL Grand Finals?

South Sydney have won the Grand Final on 17 occasions. They won their first decider in 1908 and their most recent in 2014. They have won the competition on a further four occasions in seasons where the title was decided on a first past the post basis. They were also awarded the 1909 decider on forfeit after the Balmain Tigers thought they had an agreement to boycott the match due to a scheduling dispute.

Which club has lost the most NRL Grand Finals?
The Dragons hold the record for the most lost season finales with 13. They were first beaten by Souths in 1927 and suffered their most recent Grand Final defeat in 1999 by Melbourne Storm.

Which club has the longest NRL Grand Final winning streak?
The Dragons won an incredible 11 straight deciders between 1956 and 1966. They beat five different clubs across that stretch; Balmain, Manly, Wests, Easts and Souths.

Has an NRL Grand Final always been played?
No. A deciding match has not been played on 11 separate occasions. It has however been contested in every season since 1938. That is why South Sydney have won more total premierships than St George.

Which player has won the most NRL Grand Finals?
Norm Provan won 10 Grand Finals as part of Dragons team that also won 11 consecutive titles between 1956 and 1966. Provan did not play in the team's victory in 1966.

Which player has lost the most NRL Grand Finals?
There are four players who have lost four Grand Finals each. They are Brad Fittler (1990 Panthers and 2000, 2003, 2004 Roosters), Mark Coyne (1992, 1993, 1996, 1999 Dragons), Anthony Minichiello (2000, 2003, 2004, 2010 Roosters) and Dale Finucane (2012, 2014 Bulldogs and 2016, 2018 Storm).

Which coach has won the most NRL Grand Finals?
Arthur Halloway holds the record for the coach who has won the most deciders, with eight in total. He won his first with Balmain Tigers in 1916 and his last with Eastern Suburbs in 1945.

Which coach has lost the most NRL Grand Finals?
Brian Smith holds the record with four Grand Final losses (1992, 1993 Dragons and 2001, 2010 Roosters).

Which player has scored the most points in an NRL Grand Final?
St George's Harry Bath owns the record for the most points in a decider. He scored 16 in his club's 31-9 win over Manly in 1957.

Who has scored the most tries in an NRL Grand Final?
Johnny Graves crossed the stripe on four occasions back in the 1951 finale. He helped Souths overcome Manly 42-14.

What is the biggest winning margin in an NRL Grand Final?
Manly Sea Eagles absolutely monstered Melbourne Storm in 2008. Their 40-0 victory remains the highest winning margin in an NRL Grand Final.

What is the biggest crowd in a NRL Grand Final?

107,999 fans watched Melbourne Storm come from 14-0 down to defeat the Dragons at Stadium Australia in one of the most dramatic Grand Finals ever played. That record attendance is unlikely to be broken anytime soon, with the ground's capacity now reduced to around 82,000.

Has anyone ever been sent off in an NRL Grand Final?
Phil Sigsworth is the owner of a rare piece of Australian rugby league ignominy as the only player to be sent off on Grand Final day. The Canterbury-Bankstown fullback was given his marching orders for a high tackle on Brett Kenny as his Bulldogs went down 4-2 to Parramatta Eels.

What is the NRL Grand Final trophy?

The Provan-Summons Trophy (then known as the Winfield Cup) was first presented to the winning team following the 1982 Grand Final. It is a bronze sculpture depicting a photograph taken of Norm Provan and Arthur Summons by John O'Gready, following the mud-riddled 1963 Grand Final between the Dragons and Magpies.

Who has won the most Clive Churchill Medals?
The Clive Churchill Medal for the best player in the Grand Final was first awarded in 1986. Since then, Bradley Clyde, Billy Slater and Nathan Cleary have all won the award on two occasions.

Has any player won the Clive Churchill Medal on a losing side?
Yes. Four players have been awarded the Medal despite being on a losing team. They are Bradley Clyde, Brad Mackay, Daly Cherry-Evans and Jack Wighton.

Which clubs have never won an NRL Grand Final?
Three current clubs have yet to win a decider, being New Zealand Warriors, Gold Coast Titans and the recently added Dolphins (the latter two yet to make an appearance on Grand Final day).

They join the Glebe Dirty Reds (1908-1929), Sydney University (1920-1937), Cumberland (1908), Newcastle Rebels (1908-1909), Annandale (1910-1920), Illawarra Steelers (1982-1998), Gold Coast Seagulls/Chargers (1988-1998), South Queensland Crushers (1995-1997), Western Reds (1995-1997), Adelaide Rams (1997-1998), Hunter Mariners (1997), Northern Eagles (2000-2002) to have never won a decider.

Which club has the longest NRL Grand Final losing streak?
Several clubs have lost back-to-back deciders, South Sydney (1924,1924), Newtown (1954, 1955), Parramatta (1976, 1977), Manly (1982, 1983), Balmain (1988, 1989), Dragons (1992,1993), Roosters (2003, 2004), but the record of three consecutive Grand Final losses belongs to Wests Magpies (1967, 1962, 1963).

Who has refereed the most NRL Grand Finals?
Bill Harrigan took charge of the decider on 10 separate occasions between 1989 and 2003.

How many different venues have been used for a NRL Grand Final?
The Grand Final has been played seven different grounds. The Sydney Cricket Ground has hosted the most deciders [53] while Sydney's Olympic Stadium has staged the showpiece every year since 1998, except for 2021 when the game was moved to Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

stories.headline: Case Keenum drives Chicago to 3 touchdowns as the Bears beat the Eagles 27-7
stories.summary: — Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first start in almost three years, and the Chicago Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first start in almost three years, and the Chicago Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.


Stepping in for Caleb Williams, Keenum was 24 for 34 for 247 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2019 on a 1-yard plunge with 7:19 left, capping a 13-play drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock.


It was Keenum’s first action since he started for Houston in a 36-22 loss to Cleveland on Dec. 24, 2023. Williams was sidelined by a right hamstring injury, and Tyson Bagent backed up Keenum after he cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol on Sunday.


Kalif Raymond had six receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown as Chicago (2-1) bounced back after an ugly 9-3 loss to Minnesota.


Philadelphia (2-1) turned the ball over three times and failed to record a takeaway for the third consecutive game to begin the season. Hurts was 16 for 25 for 153 yards with an interception, and Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards on 15 carries.


Keenum capped Chicago's first drive with a shovel pass to Luther Burden for an 8-yard touchdown, and he connected with a wide-open Raymond on a 41-yard TD in the second half.


Trailing 7-0, Hurts drove Philadelphia deep into Chicago territory in the second quarter before he absorbed a late hit by linebacker D'Marco Jackson along the sideline. Hurts was pulled off the field to be checked for a concussion, and backup Andy Dalton was intercepted by rookie Dillon Thieneman in the back of the end zone with 6:14 left.


Hurts scored on a quarterback sneak as time expired in the first half, but Chicago (2-1) controlled the final two periods.


Hurts was picked off by linebacker T.J. Edwards late in the third quarter. Edwards dropped a potential interception on third down on Philadelphia's first drive of the second half.


Chicago finished with 24 first downs and 128 yards rushing. The Bears had 28 first downs and 281 yards on the ground in a 24-15 win at Philadelphia last season.


Injuries
Bears: LT Braxton Jones departed with 10:22 left in the third because of a knee injury. ... Raymond was shaken up on a punt return with 3:12 remaining in the third, but he returned to the game.


Up next
Eagles: Host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.


Bears: Host the New York Jets on Sunday.

stories.headline: Yankees and Red Sox, who produce some of baseball's most memorable melodrama, meet in playoffs again
stories.summary: — Yankees-Red Sox matchups have produced plenty of melodrama, with video clips of Bucky Dent, Pedro Martínez, Aaron Boone, Curt Schilling and Dave Roberts becoming a staple of videoboards and TV broadcasts.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- — Yankees-Red Sox matchups have produced plenty of melodrama, with video clips of Bucky Dent, Pedro Martínez, Aaron Boone, Curt Schilling and Dave Roberts becoming a staple of videoboards and TV broadcasts.


Boone's 11th-inning walk-off home run for New York against Boston in Game 7 of the 2003 American League Championship Series became the defining moment of his baseball career and perhaps his life.


“I understand that a lot of people have an amazing story, a lot of those that I’ve heard, tied to that moment," the Yankees manager said Monday on the eve of his team's best-of-three Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.


Payton Tolle starts Tuesday night's opener for Boston and Cam Schlittler will be on the mound for the Yankees. This will be the seventh postseason meeting between the longtime rivals and second Wild Card Series in a row.


“A real slobberknocker,” Tolle said, using slang for a brutal fight.


New York (93-68) finished second in the AL East behind Tampa Bay (98-64), and the Red Sox (87-75) were third. The first-round winner advances to a Division Series against the Rays.


Tolle got one out in last year's Wild Card Series, a month after his major league debut.


“Walking out there to the 'pen last year, you see how much the fans interact, how bought-in they are," he said. "You see how much it means. You get to hear how loud it gets and just try and turn that into white noise the best you can.”


Yankees rookie outfielder Spencer Jones watched part of last year's matchup while driving with his girlfriend from Scranton, Pennsylvania, where he finished the season with the Yankees' Triple-A farm team, to Nashville, Tennessee.


“We stopped at a Chipotle and we just sat there and watched on the iPad,” he said.


"I’ve heard that these Wild Card Series get pretty intense, get pretty rowdy," he added. “This is going to be the most fun baseball I've ever played.”


New York hosts all three games because of its better finish in the standings. Yankee Stadium's short porch in right field could be a factor for left-handed hitters, similar to how Fenway Park's Green Monster in left is an inviting target for right-handed batters.


“I think in an ideal situation, we’re at home in front of our fans,” said Red Sox outfielder Roman Anthony, a leadoff hitter who bats from the left side. “I’m not trying to just go out there and pull home runs, right? I think for me and for everyone, it’s about getting on base and manufacturing runs.”


Judge, Stanton, Grisham are Yankees injury concerns
Aaron Judge (calf strain), Giancarlo Stanton (calf strains in both legs) and Trent Grisham (right hamstring) all took live batting practice at Yankee Stadium on Monday, hoping to be included on the series roster.


“I’ve been doing a lot of convincing, I feel like, so I’m going to keep doing that,” Judge said just after arriving at the stadium. “The most important thing is just making sure I’m healthy and ready to go for this long stretch. We’ve got another month of baseball to play.”


Crochet could be Red Sox reliever
Left-hander Garrett Crochet, who won last season's opener against the Yankees by allowing one run and four hits in 7 2/3 innings, could be a bullpen option for Boston.


He has not pitched since April 25 because of left shoulder inflammation.


“He’s worked very hard to get everything back strong the way it needs to be, but we’re still going to be evaluating him daily to see where he’s at,” manager Chad Tracy said.


Big Boston rebound
Manager Alex Cora, who led the Red Sox to the 2018 World Series title, was fired on April 25 with Boston at 10-17 and replaced by Tracy, who had been managing the Triple-A Worcester farm team.


Boston dropped to 32-46 on June 24, then went a major league-best 55-29. The Red Sox are just the fourth team to reach the postseason after dropping 14 games under .500, joining the 1914 Boston Braves and 2005 Houston Astros.


New face
Braiden Ward, a speedy 27-year-old outfielder who spent the season at Worcester, was in the Red Sox clubhouse and was assigned a locker with No. 25. He could become the seventh player to make his major league debut in the postseason.


Ward stole 61 bases in 70 attempts this year and has 272 stolen bases in 523 minor league games.


“It’s like a dream. It’s a fever dream,” he said. “One day I’m in Worcester and the next day I'm in Florida, the next day I’m at the nicest hotel we’ve ever stayed at in New York City with the greatest view, the greatest team, getting to hopefully play in the greatest rivalry.”


Cora had told Ward during spring training he could be a postseason option off the bench.


“Two of my best friends are Yankee fans, so hopefully I get to talk absolute smack to them the entire time,” he said. “I joke with the team. It’s like, how cool would it be to have your debut be Game 3, ninth inning and they’re like, `Hey Ward, you’re out there. Have fun.' So nothing crazy. No pressure.”

stories.headline: Who comes out ahead in Marchenko-Knies trade? Grading the Leafs, Blue Jackets
stories.summary: The two clubs swapped high-powered wings on the eve of opening night. Here's how each team did.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season opens on Sept. 29, but teams did not wait until opening puck drop to start improving their rosters.

The Toronto Maple Leafs and Columbus Blue Jackets completed a trade involving six players on Sept. 28, most notably sending Kirill Marchenko to Toronto and Matthew Knies to Columbus.

Throughout the season, this page will be your home for analysis of all the big deals by ESPN reporters, with the most recent swaps at the top.

Sept. 28: Marchenko to the Leafs, Knies to the Blue Jackets
Less than 24 hours before the start of a new season, the NHL had its first blockbuster trade with the Blue Jackets trading Kirill Marchenko to the Maple Leafs.

Marchenko, along with forward Miles Wood and goaltender Elvis Merzlikins, heads to Toronto in exchange for forwards Matthew Knies and Steven Lorentz, defenseman Emil Andrae and a conditional 2027 second-round pick. Columbus will retain 18% of Merzlikins' salary.

Here's a look at how both teams fared:

Toronto Maple Leafs

Grade: A-
Maybe the easiest -- and most important -- place to start is with Marchenko signing a six-year contract carrying a $12.5 million average annual value. Attaining cost certainty is always going to be key for teams, especially in this current landscape in which the price for a player's services is subject to change with each new contract. This holds true for Marchenko.

He was under contract for one more year at $3.85 million, and one more year of team control as a pending restricted free agent. That left any team acquiring him facing one of two hypotheticals:

Would it be better for them to trade for Marchenko, let him play out the season, see how he looks in their lineup and then sign him to a long-term deal?
Or do they get a sign-and-trade done so they have him locked in for several years at what they believe is a manageable cost -- at a time when every class of player is going to cash in, with top-line players at the top of that list?

Choosing the second option allowed the Leafs to avoid the seasonlong dilemma of deliberating on a long-term deal. That could prove to be a vital decision, with the expectation that Marchenko's stats are likely to surge while playing alongside Auston Matthews for at least two seasons. Because although Marchenko played with talented centers in his time with the Blue Jackets, some believe he could reach the 40-goal mark for the first time in his career playing with the Leafs superstar. His career high is 31, scored in 2024-25.

His addition sets the Leafs up to have a first line with Jack Roslovic joining Matthews and Marchenko, while having a second line featuring William Nylander, John Tavares and rookie Gavin McKenna, the Penn State forward who was the first pick in the 2026 draft.

Matthews' future is another subject for another time. Yet when it comes to Marchenko? Getting him signed long term provides the Leafs with more certainty. He is the seventh player on their active roster who has more than three years of team control remaining.

Other elements of this trade will come under question. That starts with whether it was prudent to add more to their salary cap starting next season knowing Knies, who is entering the second year of a six-year contract, was already on the roster at a cheaper salary of $7.75 million annually.

Then there are Merzlikins and Wood. Merzlikins is currently on IR after undergoing offseason shoulder surgery. He's in the final year of his contract worth $4.428 million. When healthy, he's another option for the Leafs in goal. But they could also move on from him later in the season to get help elsewhere. Wood, who went unclaimed on waivers, gives the Leafs a potential depth forward if needed.

Columbus Blue Jackets

Grade: B+
There's a challenge facing every front office that has a star player who wants out of town. Of course there will be other teams who want the player in question. Whether any of the proposed deals make sense usually ends up being the biggest hurdle to clear.

That's what makes this particular trade for the Blue Jackets one that could work. Why? Because of how they stand to benefit both now and in the future.

Moving on from Marchenko, who led the Blue Jackets with 27 goals and was second with 67 points last season, meant Columbus had to find a comparable winger in return. Knies appears to be just that. The 23-year-old, who had 23 goals and 66 points last season, gives the Blue Jackets a sizable option on the edge who can generate offensive opportunities in a top-six role. Knies will face questions about how his production will fare without Matthews, but his ability to attack the net could prove critical for a Columbus team that was in the top 10 in scoring chances per 60 minutes but was around league average in high-danger chances per 60.

Columbus could use Knies on its top line next to Adam Fantilli and Kent Johnson, while having a second line featuring Conor Garland, Sean Monahan and Valeri Nichushkin, who arrived this summer in trade.

Knies' $7.75 million AAV also helps, as Fantilli is set to earn $13.75 million annually starting this season. In total, Columbus has seven players set to make more than $7 million annually who have four or more years left on their current deals.

Beyond Knies, Lorentz provides the Blue Jackets with another proven option they can use in various spots as needed. He scored seven goals and 18 points in 71 games last season after eight and 19 in 2024-25, his first campaign with the Leafs. And while the Blue Jackets do have a bottom six in place, Lorentz gives them someone who logged more than 158 short-handed minutes last season; this could prove beneficial for a team that was 28th on the penalty kill last season.

Emil Andrae -- who was already traded once this offseason, from Philly back on June 16 -- is an option on the back end. He had 13 points in 61 games with the Flyers last season.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: Lynx's Olivia Miles unanimous WNBA Rookie of the Year
stories.summary: Olivia Miles has been named the unanimous WNBA rookie of the year, becoming the sixth player in Lynx history to earn the honor.
stories.body:
Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles has been unanimously voted the Kia WNBA Rookie of the Year.

The second overall pick in this year's draft, Miles averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds for a Lynx team that finished with the league's best record at 33-11.

Miles broke Caitlin Clark's record for most points by a rookie and was the only first-year player named to this year's All-Star Game.

Miles' efforts were key for the Lynx as star Napheesa Collier didn't make her season debut until mid-July because of offseason surgery on both ankles.

Miles is among six Minnesota players who have been named Rookie of the Year, a list that includes Crystal Dangerfield (2020), Collier (2019), Maya Moore (2011), Seimone Augusts (2006) and Betty Lennox (2000).

Miles and the Lynx hope this season still has more games left in it. Despite being the No. 1 seed in the playoffs, Minnesota is down 1-0 in its first-round series against the New York Liberty after a 91-75 loss Sunday. Miles scored 11 points and had a team-high eight rebounds in the loss.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 39
Goals: 35
Assists: 15

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami

Messi, 39, will play his final match in his national team's jersey when Argentina take on Benin in an Oct. 6 friendly at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium, following his announcement in late August that he was ending his international career. But before heading to Argentina, he gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 2

Practice One: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Saturday, October 3

Final Practice: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Sunday, October 4

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: 8 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.
